annual_compliance: Financial statements to the Centre of Registers (JAR) by 30 April; late filing draws an administrative fine (~140-1,400 EUR) and a non-compliance flag; repeated non-filing can trigger compulsory liquidation.

Fundaciones (RD 861/1986): Patronato approves cuentas anuales within 6 months of FY-end and files them with the Protectorado within 10 working days, with audit where size requires; larger ones face independent audit.

Companies file accounts at the commercial registry by the 15th day of the 7th month after FY-end (late = monetary penalties); public-benefit fundacoes send approved accounts and activity report to the SGPCM in 30 days.

ETS and social cooperatives approve annual accounts within 180 days of FY-end and file them (Registro Imprese, RUNTS) within 30 days; audit is mandatory above statutory size thresholds, with fines for late filing.

No ordinary company or charity registry exists; pontifical institutions are supervised by the Secretariat for the Economy and publish consolidated financial statements; no public annual return filing regime.

PBCs and PBFs file annual activity and financial reports with the Registrar of Non-Profits (PBFs also funding-policy reports); the Transparency Law adds quarterly foreign-funding reports; failure triggers fines.

Associations file with the Ministry of Social Development: GA resolutions in 15 days, an annual plan and an activity report on donations; budgets above JOD 2,000 require audited statements; Ministry can suspend.
Law 92/1909 is a simple declaration regime; detailed annual filing duties are unpublished, but the law prohibits undeclared associations and lets the government refuse a declaration and dissolve one.

Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (Decision 284 of 2026) sets NGO financial and auditing rules: annual budget and final accounts go to the Ministry; enforcement details are opaque and unpublished.

NGO Law 12/2010 Art. 15: each NGO sends the NGO Directorate (Interior Ministry) a financial report on fund sources and transactions plus an activity report, for the prior year by 31 March; Directorate can sanction.

CSOs file an annual budget and closing accounts with the Ministry of Human Resources, Social Development and Labour, which monitors finances; SAMA rules govern charity accounts; sanction is licence revocation.

Law 20/2008: every association must appoint an auditor (Art. 22), who sends the Ministry of Social Development a copy of the annual accounts report; books must be kept (Art. 25); Ministry can sanction.

Law 12/2004: the board presents its annual report and accounts to the general assembly; RACA (Amiri Decree 10/2020) supervises charitable institutions; major ones publish audited financial statements as standard.
Charitable societies submit an annual report, including final accounts on resources and spending, plus the annual work program to the IACAD (now the Authority for Public Benefit Organizations).

Civil Associations Law (RD 14/2000, as amended): ministry supervision includes inspection of annual account audit reports and verification of compliance with the constitution; records must be kept and available.

NGO Law 19/2006: each association keeps an annual budget; where revenues or expenses exceed BHD 10,000 the board must present final accounts to a licensed accounting firm; the Ministry supervises and can sanction.

Law 1/2001: associations submit annual administrative and financial reports to the Ministry of Social Affairs and Labour, which exercises legal and financial control supervision, with sanctions for non-compliance.

Law 1/2000 (amended 2021): annual work plan and budget to the competent ministry, then by 4 months after fiscal year-end two GA-approved reports, administrative and financial; sanctions up to dissolution.

Law 84/2014: associations file an annual activity report and financial statements with the supervising ministry (Social Affairs or Interior) by 31 March; larger ones must have accounts audited; risks suspension.

Voluntary and Humanitarian Work Act 2006 (as amended): registered organizations must re-register annually and submit annual activity and financial reports to the supervising ministry; non-filing risks revocation.
